title: Streams Knowledge Check
description: Check your understanding of readable, writable, duplex, transform streams, pipes, backpressure, and pipeline utilities.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: Why are streams useful for large files?

options.text: They process data in chunks instead of loading everything into memory

questions.explanation: Streams let Node handle large or continuous data without buffering the entire payload in memory.

questions.prompt: What does a transform stream do?

options.text: Reads input chunks, modifies them, and writes output chunks

questions.explanation: Transform streams are duplex streams that derive output from input, such as compression or parsing.

questions.prompt: What problem does backpressure help manage?

options.text: A writable destination receiving data faster than it can handle

questions.explanation: Backpressure coordinates producers and consumers so memory does not grow uncontrollably.

questions.prompt: Why is `pipeline()` preferred over manually chaining streams in many cases?

options.text: It handles completion and error propagation more reliably
It converts streams to SQL queries
It only works with HTML templates

questions.explanation: `pipeline()` wires streams together and helps manage errors and cleanup.
